title: null is a value like any other, and its key still gets renamed
prompt: What does this return? Read it — do not run it.

given.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
fun rewrite(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) })
  case a is Array -> a map rewrite($)
  else -> v
}
---
rewrite(payload)

solution:

  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []

fun rewrite(v) = v match {

  else -> v

---
rewrite(payload)

explanation.approach: `first_name`'s key is renamed even though its value is `null` — the recursion doesn't skip a key just because there was nothing to walk into. And `account_status`'s value, `"in_progress"`, keeps its underscore: only the key beside it changed.
